sections.title: Market review
sections.body:
The week to Friday 2026-09-04 was a benchmark stalemate with a violent split beneath it. SPY returned +0.1% and QQQ +0.4% over the window, but hardware and memory ripped while software and cyber were sold. Rates, credit and vol all drifted the calm way — 10-year 4.77% (-2 bp, as of 2026-09-03), high-yield OAS 2.65% (-1 bp), VIX 14.32 (-0.88 pts) — so the story was rotation inside equities, not a macro regime shift.

## Hardware led on a real print; SaaS and cyber were the mirror image
Memory/Storage (+7.6%, +7.5% vs SPY, 4 of 4 members) and Computer/GPU (+5.9%, +5.7%, 6 of 6) topped the sector board; Foundry added +5.4%. Against them, Cybersecurity fell -6.9% (-7.0% vs SPY) and Software/SaaS -4.7%. The cleanest dated anchor is DELL: it reported 2026-09-01 postmarket with EPS 6.76 versus a street mean estimate of 4.95 (basis unstated), and its +14.9% week is concentrated in the +15.8% session on 2026-09-02, the day after. That is a genuine catalyst, not beta. Coverage's rank-1 name SNDK (+17.2% week, +17.1% vs SPY) is the harder case: its gain is concentrated in a single +11.9% session on 2026-09-04 with no dated catalyst in these payloads, so I read the memory move as momentum plus AI-hardware demand narrative rather than a fact I can point to. Its last report (2026-08-05, EPS 38.82 vs 34.24 estimate) predates the window and is context only. The competing explanation for the whole hardware-versus-software split is factor rotation, not fundamentals: NVDA (+5.9%) and AMD (+2.6%) rose with the group while EDA names CDNS (-14.0%) and SNPS (-11.0%) and PANW (-10.3%) fell hard, and Semi-Cap/EDA (-1.5%) diverged from the rest of semis — a within-semi dispersion that argues something narrower than 'chips up' is at work. The observable that would settle it is whether hardware holds its bid once the earnings echo fades and whether EDA/SaaS stabilise or keep bleeding.

## Energy and ag inputs were the macro tell
Outside tech, XLE was the strongest sector ETF at +2.2% (+2.1% vs SPY) and extends a 4-week +11.4% run, alongside WTI crude at 94.09 (+2.85% on the latest snapshot). The el-nino-ag-2026 basket (DBA, MOS, NTR, DE) topped the rotation table at +6.6% for the week, +6.5% excess, with DE +10.0% and MOS +9.5% both landing in the coverage shortlist. This is the one place where a sector move and a named theme point the same direction. I treat the ag leadership as consistent with, not proof of, the El Nino supply thesis: the theme's declared triggers (NOAA ONI ≥ +0.5 for three consecutive months; CBOT corn/wheat versus 20-day) are operator-checked and I have no fresh dated reading of either, so the price is running ahead of the confirmation I can cite.

## What the calm tape does and does not tell us
The policy path prints a 55.7% probability for the 9/16 decision (as of 2026-09-04), and the SPY gamma-flip sits at 768.35 versus spot near 770.19. I note both as observations, not as evidence that dips are pre-bought or that the hike is settled — a single probability read with no prior comparison cannot carry a trend. The 2s10s and front-end rows are untested because DGS2 was not ingested, and the market-tide/flow layer returned no payload, so I am deliberately not narrating positioning or breadth this week.

Limitation: the dated close-note archive and the live headline feed both returned nothing in this run, so this article rests on the priced frame and rotation tables alone; I have not reconstructed any missing narrative.

sections.title: Outlook
sections.body:
The week ahead turns on whether the hardware-over-software split is a durable rotation or a one-week earnings echo. The strongest confirmation would be Memory/Storage and Computer/GPU holding relative strength without a fresh print to lean on, while Semi-Cap/EDA and Software/SaaS stabilise rather than extend last week's -1.5% and -4.7%. The reverse risk is symmetric and real: single-name earnings moves like DELL's 2026-09-02 jump tend to fade, and if the memory complex gives back its 2026-09-04 spike the whole 'AI hardware leadership' read weakens to momentum. Watch NVDA and the Foundry names as the tell — if they roll while EDA keeps falling, the divergence was distribution, not rotation.

ADBE reports 2026-09-10 postmarket, the one admitted dated event in the coming seven days, with a 6.93% implied move and IV rank 68.84 — elevated pricing that says the options market expects a genuine surprise, not a quiet quarter. A large move there would be the first clean read on whether the software-selloff was priced for real deterioration or overshot; I hold no directional view into it.

Energy and ag inputs are the higher-conviction persistence story. XLE's +11.4% four-week run and the ag basket's +12.9% four-week excess both argue the move has legs beyond one week, and crude near 94 supports it. The condition that confirms continuation is crude holding its bid and the ag names (DE, MOS) keeping relative strength; the condition that invalidates it is a crude reversal or the ag basket losing its excess as the El Nino narrative stalls without a fresh ONI or CBOT reading to renew it. Because I cannot cite a current trigger observation, I treat the ag leadership as a price fact to monitor, not a thesis to press.

On the macro frame, the 9/16 decision is later context, not a coming-week event, but its 55.7% probability is the backdrop that keeps rates (4.77%), credit (2.65%) and vol (14.32%) quiet. The observable that would break the calm is any of those three moving off its recent range; absent that, the base case is continued intra-equity rotation with the index going nowhere. I am not forecasting the front end or the curve — those rows are untested for lack of DGS2 — and I am not reading breadth, since the flow layer had no payload.
